title: The Efficacy and Safety of a Radial Approach versus a Distal Radial Approach for Diagnostic Coronary Angiography and Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis (protocol)
author: Toshihide Izumida
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bramm2c6

steps.title: Define Study Population and Inclusion Criteria
steps.instruction: Identify adult patients (18 years of age or older) of either gender undergoing diagnostic coronary angiography (CA) and percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for coronary artery disease (CAD).

substeps.instruction: Exclude patients requiring a sheath larger than 7 Fr.

steps.title: Perform Distal Radial Approach (DRA)
steps.instruction: Access the coronary arteries using the distal radial approach technique.

substeps.instruction: Puncture the distal radial arteries at the proximal part of the anatomical snuffbox or the first intermetacarpal space.
Pass a guidewire smoothly through the needle after successful puncture.
Use the guidewire to guide the sheath through the artery.
Perform diagnostic CA and PCI through the introduced sheath.

steps.title: Perform Radial Approach (RA) Control
steps.instruction: Access the coronary arteries using the standard radial approach by puncturing the radial artery at the forearm, a few centimeters above the wrist joint.

steps.title: Search for Eligible Studies
steps.instruction: Conduct a comprehensive search for randomized-controlled trials (RCTs) across multiple databases and resources regardless of language, country, or publication year.

substeps.instruction: Search electronic databases: Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), MEDLINE via PubMed, and EMBASE via ProQuest Dialog.
Search for ongoing or unpublished trials via World Health Organization International Clinical Trials Platform Search Portal (ICTRP) and ClinicalTrials.gov.
Review reference lists of international guidelines (ESC, NICE, ACC/AHA), eligible studies, and articles citing eligible studies.
Contact original authors for unpublished or additional data.

steps.title: Screen and Select Studies
steps.instruction: Evaluate the eligibility of identified articles using two independent reviewers (TI and RY).

substeps.instruction: Screen titles and abstracts.
Assess eligibility based on full-text review.
Resolve disagreements via discussion or by a third reviewer (JW) acting as an arbiter.

steps.title: Extract Data
steps.instruction: Perform independent data extraction using a standardized collection form.

substeps.instruction: Pre-check the form using 10 randomly selected studies.
Extract information on study design, study population, interventions, and outcomes.
Resolve disagreements via discussion or by a third reviewer (JW).

steps.title: Assess Risk of Bias
steps.instruction: Evaluate the risk of bias in included studies independently using the Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool.

substeps.instruction: Perform evaluation with two reviewers (TI and RY).
Resolve disagreements via discussion or by a third reviewer (JW).

steps.title: Analyze Treatment Effects
steps.instruction: Pool data to measure the efficacy and safety of DRA versus RA.

substeps.instruction: Pool relative risk ratios and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for binary variables: successful cannulation rate, radial artery spasm (RAS), and radial artery occlusion (RAO).
Pool mean differences and 95% CIs for continuous variables: mean number of punctures per patient and mean time for hemostasis.
Summarize all adverse events based on original article definitions (without meta-analysis).

steps.title: Handle Missing Data and Statistics
steps.instruction: Address missing information to ensure analysis robustness.

substeps.instruction: Request missing data from original authors.
Perform intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis for dichotomous data.
Do not impute missing continuous data per Cochrane handbook recommendations.
Calculate standard deviation from standard error or p-values using the Altman method, or from CI and t-value using the Cochrane handbook/validated methods if values are missing.

steps.title: Evaluate Heterogeneity and Reporting Bias
steps.instruction: Assess the consistency of results and the potential for publication bias.

substeps.instruction: Evaluate statistical heterogeneity via visual inspection of forest plots and the I2 statistic.
Perform Cochrane Chi2 test (Q-test) if I2 > 50% (significance set at P < 0.10).
Assess publication bias via visual inspection of funnel plots and the Egger test (only if 10 or more trials are available).

steps.title: Perform Meta-Analysis
steps.instruction: Execute the meta-analysis using Review Manager software (RevMan 5.4.1) utilizing a random-effects model.

steps.title: Conduct Subgroup and Sensitivity Analyses
steps.instruction: Perform additional analyses to test the robustness of primary outcomes.

substeps.instruction: Subgroup analysis by age (under 65 vs 65 and over), approach side (right vs left), and procedure type (diagnostic CA vs PCI).
Sensitivity analysis by excluding studies using imputed statistics.
Sensitivity analysis using only participants who completed the study with complete data.

steps.title: Generate Summary of Findings
steps.instruction: Create a Summary of Findings table based on the Cochrane handbook.

substeps.instruction: Include outcomes: successful cannulation rates, RAS, RAO, number of punctures, and mean time for hemostasis.
Apply GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation) approach to evaluate the quality of evidence.
